column7: 2026-11-06: parseBytes (named export) supports only plain numbers/B and binary KiB..YiB, case-sensitive. kB/MB/GB etc deliberately unsupported (throw SyntaxError) until the user hears back from the storage team on how to read them. My choices: accepts optional sign/surrounding whitespace/nbsp separator; fractional bytes not rounded; throws TypeError for non-strings.

2026-11-06: Storage team answer: on this branch (storage-app) parseBytes must read the non-i units as powers of 1024 (Windows Explorer style): '1 KB' or '1 kB' = 1024, '1 MB' = 1048576, and so on. Not implemented yet; the user will add it next session. Until then they still throw SyntaxError. Whether other casings (e.g. 'kb') are accepted was not decided; ask.

2026-11-06: billing-svc: parseBytes already implemented (commit 0898691): plain numbers/B and KiB..YiB, case-sensitive; kB/MB/GB throw SyntaxError. The storage-app rule (non-i units = powers of 1024) is specific to that branch and must NOT be applied here; billing hasn't specified decimal units.

2026-11-06: billing-svc: when decimal units (kB, MB, GB...) are added on this branch they must be strict SI, powers of 1000 (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes), matching what prettyBytes prints. Stated by the user (billing quotes in SI). Overrides the storage-app 1024 reading for this branch only. Not implemented yet; they still throw SyntaxError.

2026-11-06: parseBytes now implemented: kB/KB/MB/GB.. = powers of 1024 (storage team, Windows Explorer style). My choice (not user-decided): other casings like 'kb', 'mb', 'Kb' still throw SyntaxError; only 'kB' and 'KB' accepted for kilo. Documented in readme + index.d.ts.
